A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TestGenEval study. Text, tables, figures and Appendices A-H are readable and can be matched across the reorganization without material gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original execution-based evaluations of generated tests, including pass rates, coverage and mutation scores in Tables 2-3 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 reports original test-generation and completion evaluations in Tables 2-3 and Appendix E, together with empirical analyses in Appendices F-G.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, generation and completion procedures, and Appendix C prompts are retained. Replacing class under test with file under test clarifies the existing file-level task rather than changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 1,210 code-test pairs from 11 Python repositories and the 160-pair Lite subset. Full-suite generation and first, last and extra test completion remain unchanged, as do the benchmark-correlation comparisons.

E2.justification: The same ten model configurations appear in corresponding full and Lite comparisons, covering CodeLlama, Gemma, Llama 3.1, DeepSeekCoder, Codestral and GPT-4o. Newly cited mutation-testing research does not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Filtering, prompting, context truncation, temperatures, metrics and sampling/context experiments are retained. Any pass@1 renames an already defined metric. The added mutation-operator description documents an existing evaluation rather than reporting a changed protocol.

E4.justification: The correlation, sampling, context-length, error and frontier analyses already appear in v1. v2 Appendix F.6 collects the three qualitative comparisons previously in Section 4.2; the existing error and frontier sections become F.7-F.8. Redisplayed plots add no new analyses.

E5.justification: Appendix G retains the confidence intervals, noise statistics and pairwise-comparison reporting. No new run-count, seed or statistical procedure is reported. The added 1.06% mutation-uncertainty statement is consistent with the previously reported 1.1% at finer precision.

E6.justification: Corresponding result tables and appendix plots retain their values and findings. For example, Table 2 still gives GPT-4o 35.2% coverage and 18.8% mutation score, and Table 3 retains Codestral's 74.3% last-test pass@5. Relocated examples and repeated plots report existing results.

T1.justification: The metric definitions retain their meaning despite the Any pass@1 terminology change. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs, and the added mutation-tool description introduces no mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same benchmark scope, novelty claims and conclusions about difficulty generating high-quality tests. No new core contribution or stronger performance claim is introduced.

C2.justification: The explanations concerning execution reasoning, mocking, context and limited coverage gains remain. Section 5 and Appendix H retain the limitations concerning contamination, overfitting, file-level context, missing agentic baselines and mutation-testing cost.

D1.justification: Appendix D.2.1 now identifies Cosmic Ray, provides tool and operator links, and specifies its default mutation operators without filtering. v1 only referred to selecting mutations according to best practices. This improves documentation of the existing evaluation.

R1.justification: v2 adds Sanchez et al. (2022) and Deb et al. (2024) to support its mutation-testing tool discussion. Section 2.2 also refines the connection to Rao et al.'s method-level generation work. The broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 4.1 gains separate correlation, sampling and context subsections, while detailed qualitative comparisons are collected in Appendix F.6. This localized reorganization accompanies terminology and citation-style edits, conference headers and acknowledgments; most prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: The main analysis is substantially reorganized visually: v2 Figures 6-8 repeat plots from v1 Figures 16, 26 and 27 beside their discussion, while two qualitative examples move to Appendix F.6 and the retained example is also repeated there. Figures 1-2 become sharper graphics, and Tables 2 and 6 clarify pass-column labels. These changes substantially alter presentation without adding empirical evidence.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility by identifying Cosmic Ray and its unfiltered default operators, clarifies Any pass@1, and makes existing quantitative evidence easier to inspect beside the main discussion. Moving examples reduces their main-text prominence but preserves them in the appendix. The gains are useful and limited; the scientific evidence and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
